title: Microbatch Sentinel: adaptive backoff and KV spill strategy for sustained high-QPS
creator: Ava Patel
description:
Problem: Under sustained high QPS (multi-tenant and bursty patterns), we observe frequent headroom exhaustion on GPUs caused by the interaction of micro-batch thresholds and KV cache working set growth. This triggers hard backpressure that spikes tail latencies and increases request rejection rates.

Goal: Implement a Microbatch Sentinel subsystem that dynamically adjusts admission thresholds and coordinates a graded KV spill/eviction path to maintain tail latency SLOs while maximizing throughput. The sentinel should be conservative about forcing RPC-level rejections, prefer soft-degrades (graceful slowdowns, slot leasing, spill-to-host), and provide observable telemetry for rollback.

Proposed approach:
1) Per-GPU Reservoir Estimator - continuous estimate of usable GPU memory for active KV and batch buffers with hysteresis and uncertainty margin (configured by percentile, default 95th).
2) Working-Set Hotness Predictor - lightweight exponential moving average on key access counts + LRU age histogram to estimate KV hit probability at candidate retention levels.
3) Sentinel Admission Controller - a small control loop that adjusts microbatch admission_threshold and soft_window_size based on reservoir estimate, predicted hit-probability, and recent latency tail. It implements graded degrade levels (G0-G3):
   - G0: normal operation
   - G1: gentle batching delay (10-40ms hold) + tighten batching window
   - G2: slot leasing for low-priority requests and partial spill-to-host for cold KV pages
   - G3: selective request reroute to low-latency fallback models or temporary reject under strict SLAs
4) KV Spill/Async Evict - non-blocking eviction pipeline that moves cold KV shards to pinned host memory and (optionally) compressed format; accessible via an async IO path to minimize GPU stalls.
5) Safety and Rollback - circuit-breakers on tail latency, drop in successful generation rate, and OOM events. Canary rollout with automatic rollback if p95 latency increases >20% or error rate >0.5% absolute.

Trade-offs and rationale: We prefer soft-degrade to protect user-facing latency; some increase in cold-call CPU/host IO is acceptable if it reduces GPU OOMs and rejections. The predictor errs on the side of evicting more aggressively for large multi-model servers where KV contention is high.

Metrics to track:
- p50/p95/p99 generation latency per model
- microbatch size distribution and admission rejections per minute
- KV hit rate and effective working-set size
- GPU memory headroom percentile and #evictions/sec
- Rate of spill-to-host IO and CPU utilization

Non-goals: This ticket is not implementing cross-node global KV sharding or any new persistent storage layer; scope is controller + local spill/evict + observability.
acceptance_criteria: Sentinel control loop can run in steady state without causing >1% additional CPU utilization on the runtime host
p95 latency for canonical high-QPS synthetic trace remains within 10% of baseline while throughput is within 90% of pre-surge capacity
System can perform non-blocking KV spill with <30ms median additional tail penalty for cold-key misses
Canary rollout demonstrates automatic rollback on configured threshold breaches (p95 +20% or error rate +0.5%)
Comprehensive dashboards and alerts added: KV hit rate, reservoir headroom, sentinel degrade level, and evictions/sec

risks: Incorrect working-set predictor tuning may cause over-eviction and increase repeat cold misses
Host IO spikes from spill path could affect co-located services if not throttled
Complexity of graded degrade may introduce edge cases where priority inversion causes high-priority requests to be delayed
rollout_plan: 1) Merge behind feature flag and run internal perf harness on dedicated perf cluster
2) Canary on 2 low-traffic regions with 5% of traffic for 24h monitoring the acceptance metrics
3) Gradually increase canary to 25% with automated rollback guardrails
4) Full rollout if steady for 72h; otherwise iterate on predictor thresholds and evict heuristics
5) Post rollout: observe for 2 weeks and capture memory/latency drift; follow-up ticket for any tuning
